subject: Behavioral Economics
title: The Pre-Mortem Technique
description: A 60-second lesson on The Pre-Mortem Technique.

hook.text: Before launching the project, the team imagined it had already failed. Then they asked: why?

buildup.text: Klein's pre-mortem flips optimism bias. Instead of asking what could go right, you start with failure.

discovery.text: This technique surfaces risks people are too polite or optimistic to mention in normal planning.

twist.text: Teams that pre-mortem identify 30% more risks than teams that brainstorm risks the standard way.

climax.text: Starting from failure gives permission to be critical. That permission is the real breakthrough.

punchline.text: Imagine failure first. Prevent it second.

quiz.question: What does a pre-mortem do differently from standard risk planning?
options: It only looks at financial risks
It starts from imagined failure to surface hidden risks
